name: bernstein_vazirani_secret_01
description: The Bernstein-Vazirani lesson's fixed example: a 1 on q0, a 0 on q1 (printed 01).

code.qiskit:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

qc = QuantumCircuit(3, 2)
qc.x(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.h(1)
qc.h(2)
qc.cx(0, 2)
qc.h(0)
qc.h(1)
qc.measure(0, 0)
qc.measure(1, 1)
code.cirq:
import cirq

q = cirq.LineQubit.range(3)
# Cirq lists q[0] first in a state; Qiskit lists qubit 0 last. The circuit is the same.
circuit = cirq.Circuit(
    cirq.X(q[2]),
    cirq.H(q[0]),
    cirq.H(q[1]),
    cirq.H(q[2]),
    cirq.CNOT(q[0], q[2]),
    cirq.H(q[0]),
    cirq.H(q[1]),
    cirq.measure(q[0], key="c0"),
    cirq.measure(q[1], key="c1"),
)
code.pennylane:
import pennylane as qml

dev = qml.device("default.qubit", wires=3)


@qml.qnode(dev)
def circuit():
    qml.PauliX(wires=2)
    qml.Hadamard(wires=0)
    qml.Hadamard(wires=1)
    qml.Hadamard(wires=2)
    qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 2])
    qml.Hadamard(wires=0)
    qml.Hadamard(wires=1)
    # measured: q0 -> c0, q1 -> c1
    return qml.probs(wires=[0, 1])
